applications.explanationEn: Querríamos uses the polite first-person-plural form for making a softened request.
Por favor adds the conventional politeness marker to the request.

regions.labelEs: TOME. ESTOS ARTÍCULOS SOBRE EL PROBLEMA DE LA MOCHILA PUEDEN AYUDARLE.

applications.explanationEn: Tome is the usted command form used to tell one person formally to take something.
Pueden changes for the plural subject, while ayudar remains in its dictionary form with le attached.
Ayudarle writes the unchanged verb ayudar and the formal object word le together as one word.

regions.labelEs: ESCUCHE, TENGO OTRAS SEIS MESAS QUE...

applications.explanationEn: Escuche is the usted command form used to ask one person formally to listen.

regions.labelEs: LO MÁS RÁPIDO POSIBLE, POR SUPUESTO. ¿QUIERE ALGO SOBRE EL VIAJANTE?

applications.explanationEn: Lo más and posible frame rápido as the quality being pushed to the greatest practical degree.
Por supuesto marks the speaker's ready agreement that this requirement is obvious.
Quiere uses the same singular form as él or ella while addressing the customer formally as usted.

cards.noteEn: Hobby is an English loanword used in Spanish. A common Spanish alternative is afición or pasatiempo.

example.en: Photography is my hobby.

cards.answerEn: to introduce; to insert or embed
cards.noteEn: Introducir can mean putting something into a larger setting, not only introducing one person to another.

example.es: Introdujeron una regla nueva en el juego.
example.en: They introduced a new rule into the game.

cards.answerEn: problems whose proposed solutions are quick to check but which have no known efficient general solver
cards.noteEn: NP-complete problems are the hardest problems in the class NP, in a precise sense: every NP problem can be efficiently translated into any NP-complete problem. If an efficient general algorithm were found for one of them, it would efficiently solve every problem in NP. No such algorithm is currently known.
NP is an international computer-science abbreviation. It groups decision problems whose proposed solutions can be checked efficiently.

example.en: The problem belongs to NP.

cards.noteEn: The ending -os makes completos match the masculine plural noun problemas. After NP-, it forms the technical description NP-completos.

example.en: These problems are NP-complete.

cards.answerEn: Use al followed by the action verb in its dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form ends in -ar, -er, or -ir and is called the infinitive. Al + verb tells when the main action happens. Translate it naturally as “when,” “on,” or “upon”: al llegar means “when arriving” or simply “when someone arrives.”
cards.questionEn: How do you say “when doing something” or “upon doing something”?

example.en: When I arrive, I will call you.

cards.noteEn: At a restaurant, pedir is the ordinary verb for ordering food or drink. The same verb can mean asking for or requesting something elsewhere.

example.en: I am going to order the soup.

cards.promptEs: problema de la mochila · suma exacta
cards.answerEn: select a subset of available items that obeys a limit or hits an exact target
cards.noteEn: The classic knapsack problem chooses items with weights and values under a capacity limit. Asking which menu prices add to one exact total is more specifically the closely related subset-sum problem. The decision versions are NP-complete, so the restaurant request hides a computationally difficult search inside an ordinary order.

cards.questionEn: What common menu phrase means French fries or chips?
cards.noteEn: In Spain, patatas fritas commonly names fried potatoes and often means French fries on a restaurant menu; context can also indicate potato chips. Many Latin American varieties use papas fritas.

example.es: Pedimos una hamburguesa con patatas fritas.
example.en: We ordered a hamburger with French fries.

cards.noteEn: On a menu, individual says that an item is sized or intended for one person rather than for sharing.

example.en: We ordered two individual portions.

cards.noteEn: Alitas is the plural diminutive of alas, “wings.” On a menu it commonly refers to chicken wings.

example.en: The wings are spicy.

cards.questionEn: What Spanish menu phrase means chicken wings?
cards.noteEn: Alitas literally means “little wings,” and de pollo identifies the meat. Together they form the ordinary menu name for chicken wings.

example.en: We shared some chicken wings.

cards.noteEn: Palitos is a diminutive plural of palos. For food, it describes small stick-shaped pieces.

example.en: She cut the carrot into sticks.

cards.questionEn: What Spanish menu phrase means mozzarella sticks?
cards.noteEn: Palitos names small stick-shaped pieces, and de mozzarella says what they contain. The complete phrase is a conventional name for mozzarella sticks.

example.es: Los palitos de mozzarella vienen con salsa.
example.en: The mozzarella sticks come with sauce.

cards.noteEn: Variado normally describes something as varied or assorted. Used alone on a menu, it can name a mixed selection or sampler plate.

example.en: We ordered an assortment of cheeses.

cards.answerEn: sandwiches (printed without the standard Spanish accent)
cards.noteEn: Standard Spanish spelling is sándwiches, with an accent on the first a. This printed menu omits that accent, so the card preserves the exact surface form while showing the usual spelling here.

example.en: We ordered two sandwiches.

cards.noteEn: Querríamos is a courteous form of querer, “to want.” It softens an order or request in much the same way as English “we would like.”

example.es: Querríamos una mesa junto a la ventana.
example.en: We would like a table by the window.

cards.questionEn: How do you politely say “I would like” or “we would like” when requesting something?
cards.answerEn: Use querría for one speaker or querríamos for “we,” then name what is wanted.
cards.noteEn: These polite forms come from querer, “to want.” The middle changes to querr-, and the endings -ía or -íamos express “would.” They make an order or request less direct than quiero or queremos.

example.en: I would like a coffee, please.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of por favor (“please”)

cards.noteEn: Por favor makes a request more polite. It can appear before or after the request.

example.en: Close the door, please.

cards.noteEn: Eh can fill a pause while a speaker thinks or reacts. Its tone and punctuation determine whether it sounds hesitant, surprised, or attention-getting.

example.en: Um... I need to think about it.

cards.noteEn: Tome tells one person addressed as usted to take something. In a handover, it can work like English “here you go.”

example.en: Take this document, please.

cards.answerEn: Use the usted command form: regular -ar verbs end in -e, while regular -er and -ir verbs end in -a.
cards.noteEn: Usted is the polite or formal singular “you.” Hablar becomes hable, comer becomes coma, and escribir becomes escriba. Usted is usually left out because the command ending already shows formal address. Some common verbs are irregular, such as decir → diga.
cards.questionEn: How do you politely tell one person to do something in Spanish?

example.en: Come in, please.

cards.noteEn: In academic or technical contexts, un artículo can be a scholarly paper rather than a newspaper article or a grammatical article.

example.en: I read two scientific papers.

cards.noteEn: Mochila is the everyday word for a backpack. In el problema de la mochila, it supplies the Spanish name of the computer-science knapsack problem.

example.es: Guardé el libro en la mochila.
example.en: I put the book in the backpack.

cards.answerEn: they can; they are able to

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.

example.en: We can enter now.

cards.noteEn: Ayudar is the unchanged dictionary form, and le means the formal listener here. Spanish attaches le to the end of an unchanged verb and writes ayudarle as one word.

example.en: I want to help you.

cards.promptEs: verbo en forma de diccionario + pronombre unido
cards.questionEn: Where can a short object word such as me, te, lo, or la go with an unchanged action verb?
cards.answerEn: Attach it to the end of the verb and write the result as one word.
cards.noteEn: An unchanged dictionary-form verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Short object words can attach directly: conocer + te becomes conocerte, and ayudar + me becomes ayudarme.

example.en: I want to help you.

cards.noteEn: Escuche tells one person addressed as usted to listen. The informal command to a friend would be escucha.

example.en: Listen to this explanation, please.

cards.noteEn: Otras goes before a feminine plural noun. Spanish normally does not put un or una before otro or otra in this meaning.

example.en: We are looking for other answers.

cards.answerEn: find the shortest route that visits every required stop
cards.noteEn: The traveling-salesperson problem asks for the shortest tour through a set of locations. Comparing all possible routes becomes difficult as the number of stops grows; its decision version is NP-complete. Visiting several restaurant tables as quickly as possible supplies the comic's second example.
Que connects a noun to information describing it. Depending on the noun, English translates it as “who,” “that,” or “which.”

example.es: La persona que llamó es mi amiga.
example.en: The person who called is my friend.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins lo más... posible (“as... as possible”)
cards.noteEn: Lo stays unchanged in this degree expression. It works with más and posible around the description being maximized.

example.en: Make it as simple as possible.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something should be as fast, simple, close, or otherwise extreme as possible?
cards.answerEn: Use lo más, then the description, then posible.
cards.noteEn: Lo and posible stay fixed around the description being pushed to its greatest practical degree. The middle word can describe a quality or manner, as in lo más claro posible or lo más pronto posible.

example.en: Explain it as clearly as possible.

cards.answerEn: most; part of lo más... posible (“as... as possible”)
cards.noteEn: Más raises the degree of the description between lo and posible. The complete pattern is translated naturally with “as... as possible,” not word by word.

example.en: Leave as soon as possible.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of por supuesto (“of course”)

cards.questionEn: How do you say “of course” when something is obvious or agreed?
cards.noteEn: Por supuesto is a fixed expression. It can confirm a request or emphasize that the speaker sees something as expected.

example.en: Of course, you can come in.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of por supuesto (“of course”)
do you want; would you like (formal singular)
cards.noteEn: Quiere is the present form used for usted, the formal singular “you.” The same written form can also mean “he or she wants”; context identifies the person.

example.en: Would you like to see the menu, sir?

cards.answerEn: Use the same singular verb form used with él or ella (“he” or “she”).
cards.noteEn: Although usted refers to the listener, Spanish treats it like “he” or “she” when choosing the verb. Compare tú necesitas for informal “you need” with usted necesita for formal “you need.” Spanish often leaves usted unspoken when the context makes it clear.
cards.questionEn: When usted means polite or formal “you,” which verb form goes with it?

example.en: Do you need help? (formal)

cards.noteEn: A viajante travels for work, traditionally to sell goods. El problema del viajante is the conventional Spanish name for the traveling-salesperson problem in computer science.

example.en: The traveling salesperson visited five cities.
